bigPicture: AI agents stopped being demos and started doing real unsupervised work — discovering architecture improvements humans missed, managing ad campaigns, reviewing PRs — while the industry scrambles to build the security, eval, and legal guardrails to keep up.

dataPoints.context: Karpathy's autoresearch agent ran unsupervised and found real, generalizable architecture discoveries
LeCun's European AI startup raises largest seed ever, betting against the LLM paradigm

dataPoints.stat: 32% of dev candidates hurt by AI coding tools
dataPoints.context: AI-assisted coding backfiring in interviews — dependency risks surfacing in hiring data
OpenAI buys Promptfoo, Claude Code embeds in Perplexity, Gemini embeds in Drive — consolidation accelerating

tldr: Agentic research crosses a threshold: Karpathy's autoresearch found 20 real architecture improvements unsupervised, validated on held-out data — agents are now doing science, not just code.
The agent stack is consolidating fast: Claude Code inside Perplexity, OpenAI acquiring Promptfoo, Google embedding Gemini in Drive — standalone tools are becoming features.
AI safety hits the courtroom: Anthropic sues the Pentagon over military AI use, backed by OpenAI and Google employees — the first real industry-wide line in the sand.
Enterprise AI shifts from novelty to workflow: GPT-5.4 converting finance users on spreadsheets, Perplexity running ad campaigns autonomously, LangChain dogfooding GTM agents.

The human cost is getting concrete: 32% of devs hurt in interviews by AI dependency, workers literally generating training data for their own replacement — the labor reckoning isn't theoretical anymore.
